correctness.rationale: Finite Esakia duality sends the (2^m+1)-element top extension of Boolean P([m]) to the rooted star P_m. A p-morphism P_n→P_m sends source root either to a target leaf (forcing constant map, m choices and two-valued algebra image) or to target root (forcing a surjective function of n leaves onto m leaves, m! S(n,m) possibilities and injective algebra map). Surjective p-morphic quotients of P_m are singleton or rooted stars with k≤m leaves, and their fibers are partitions of the original leaves; this proves the exact Bell-graded subalgebra spectrum and inclusion order by coarsening. For n=m, bijections give m! automorphisms; m leaf constants give the only other endomorphisms and are idempotent; only identity is an idempotent permutation, yielding m+1 idempotents but just two distinct retract images. We reconstructed dual upcone conditions and verified small m,n counts against independent direct algebra implication/residuation reasoning. The source standard-library program exhaustively enumerates n,m≤5 p-morphisms and m≤4 all subalgebras; that finite enumeration does not stand in for the all-parameter argument.

evidence: General Esakia duality applies to every finite Heyting algebra but requires classifying the star maps; it does not itself supply the m+m!S(n,m) image-rank polynomial.
